QuestionStmt.S: A string of mass 0.1 kg/m has length 0.9 m. It is fixed at both ends and stretched such that it has a tension of 40 N. The string vibrates in three segments with amplitude 0.3 cm. The amplitude (maximum) of the particle velocity is (in m/s)

Solution.S:
Given: μ = 0.1 kg/m, L = 0.9 m, T = 40 N, n = 3 segments (3rd harmonic), A = 0.3 cm = 0.003 m.

Step 1: Wave speed on string
v = √(T/μ) = √(40/0.1) = √400 = 20 m/s

Step 2: Frequency of nth harmonic for fixed ends
f_n = n v / (2L)
For n = 3: f = 3 × 20 / (2 × 0.9) = 60 / 1.8 = 100/3 Hz

Step 3: Angular frequency
ω = 2πf = 2π × (100/3) = 200π/3 rad/s

Step 4: Maximum particle velocity
v_max = A × ω = 0.003 × (200π/3) = (0.6π)/3 = 0.2π = π/5 m/s

Thus, amplitude of particle velocity = π/5 m/s.

Correct option: C
